fields.label: Mechanism
fields.value: The OS decides when applications receive CPU time and how much memory/resources they receive.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Prevents a single application from monopolizing limited hardware and enables concurrent application execution.

fields.label: Conditions
fields.value: Multiple applications contend for finite CPU and memory resources.

fields.label: Inverse or converse
fields.value: Without allocation, one program could monopolize resources.

record.inverse_or_converse: Without allocation, one program could monopolize resources.

fields.label: Mechanism
fields.value: The OS separates applications so errors and security vulnerabilities in one application are contained while communication remains possible.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Improves reliability and security without eliminating application communication.

fields.label: Conditions
fields.value: Isolation must coexist with controlled inter-application communication.

record.mechanism: The OS separates applications so errors and security vulnerabilities in one application are contained while communication remains possible.

fields.label: Mechanism
fields.value: OS interfaces hide hardware-access details such as physical memory behind standardized services/interfaces.

fields.label: Conditions

fields.label: Mechanism
fields.value: OS exposes reusable interfaces for networking, disks and other common facilities.

fields.label: Effect
fields.value: Applications can run across different hardware without being rewritten for each hardware implementation.

fields.label: Inverse or converse
fields.value: Missing services can force applications to depend on hardware-specific implementations.
